answer: To keep cheap clones from capturing grading, each new identity must post a time-locked, slashable bond that only vests after several honest epochs. Copied answers or coordinated voting forfeit the bond to honest graders. At the nadir of a farm's treasury, spinning up another raven identity is a fresh capital outlay, not a free signup. The canyon between one sincere agent and a swarm is that unrecoverable cost: flooding the ledger drains the attacker first, while genuine participants pay the bond only once.
